bullets.title: FOXA: UBS upgrades to Buy; Q1 beats by 22%+ on World Cup, political ads, Tubi strength
bullets.body: Fox Corp. F1Q27 revenue came in at $4.57B (+22% YoY), beating consensus of $4.29B, while adj. EBITDA of $1.64B (+54% YoY) beat by ~22%. TV advertising surged 60% YoY driven by World Cup, record political ad spend (expected $350M+ for midterm cycle), and Tubi growing 35% YoY. UBS upgraded to Buy; Citi maintains Buy at $78 PT (23% upside); Wolfe maintains Outperform at $93. Pending Roku acquisition ($22B, $160/share, H1 2027 close) awaiting DOJ HSR clearance after shareholder approvals received.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: $115B all-stock merger announced; JPM suspends LITE rating as deal advisor
bullets.body: Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal at 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share, implying ~$115B enterprise value — one of the largest tech deals ever. Deal targets close by March 31, 2028; requires shareholder and regulatory approvals including SAMR review. Management targets >$1B annual run-rate synergies with EPS/margin accretion starting 2029; combined TAM expands to $550B. LITE was -4.4% and MRVL -2.3% pre-market. JPM suspended its LITE rating/PT ($1,280 prior) due to conflict as MRVL financial advisor. UBS rates MRVL Buy ($350 PT) and LITE Neutral ($960 PT).

bullets.title: META: Massive capital raise — multi-tranche bonds + $5B equity purchase interest from NVDA/AMD/AVGO
bullets.body: Meta is holding investor calls for a potential five-part USD and six-part EUR bond offering, with Citi and Morgan Stanley as leads. NVIDIA, AMD, and Broadcom have indicated interest in purchasing up to $5.0B of Meta Class A common stock. Meta expects $135-$145B capex in 2026 and plans a $60B ATM program for Q1 2027. S&P revised Meta's outlook from stable to negative citing high capex and negative FCF.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Wells Fargo cuts search revenue estimates as AI Overviews penetration hits 82%
bullets.body: Wells Fargo cut FY27/FY28 search revenue growth estimates by ~2pts each to +7.7%/+9.6%, projecting paid clicks growth of +4% in 4Q26 and 0% in 1Q27, with recovery only in 2Q27. AI Overviews penetration reached 82% globally (up ~7pts in October), driving a -0.97 correlation between paid clicks/session and US desktop AI Overviews penetration. Maintains Overweight with $365 PT; FY27/FY28 EPS cut 2% each to $14.60/$17.79.

bullets.title: AAPL: F4Q26 earnings tonight; iPhone demand/ASPs and DRAM cost pressures are key watch items
bullets.body: Street expects F4Q26 revenue of $113.4B, gross margin of 47.5% (includes ~100bps tariff refund benefit; ex-tariffs 46.5%, down ~70bps YoY on higher DRAM costs), and EPS of $1.99. iPhone growth expected to decelerate to ~14% YoY from 22-23% prior quarters on ~5% fewer units. UBS flags Services at $31.6B (+10% YoY). New CEO John Ternus's first call will be closely watched for AI/Siri strategy. Hedgeye's McCullough keeps AAPL on long list heading into print.

bullets.title: PLTR: UBS bullish into earnings — demand exceeds supply, 51x 2027 FCF at 90%+ growth profile
bullets.body: UBS rates PLTR with high conviction (8.5/10 sentiment) ahead of earnings, citing AI enterprise demand materially exceeding supply and competitive advantages in operational AI, model fine-tuning, and sovereign AI. FQ3 guidance is $2.16-2.164B revenue with op income of $1.292-1.296B; FY26 revenue guided $8.15-8.158B. McCullough keeps PLTR as a favored name into earnings.

bullets.title: AMD: Expects high end of FQ3 guidance ($13.1-13.3B range); Wolfe hosting post-earnings webcast 11/4
bullets.body: AMD is expected to report at the high end of FQ3 guidance of $13.1-13.3B per UBS. Wolfe Research is hosting a post-earnings webcast with management callback on 11/4 at 10:30am ET hosted by Chris Caso.

bullets.title: ALAB: UBS raises 4Q estimates; Trainium 3 volume up 15% QoQ, Orion addressing neocloud customers
bullets.body: UBS modestly raises ALAB's 4Q EPS estimate on lower OpEx; 4Q revenue growth expected ~20% QoQ with 3Q revenue/EPS unchanged at $557M/$1.21 and 4Q raised to $668M/$1.42. Trainium 3 units increase ~15% QoQ from 0.6-0.7M to 0.7-0.8M. C2028 revenue/EPS revised down slightly to $3,789M/$7.36 from $4,007M/$7.69. Orion rack architecture targets neoclouds and AWS alternative customers.

bullets.title: MU: DRAM pricing +12% M/M, +15.5% Q/Q in October; KeyBanc maintains OW at $1,750 PT
bullets.body: KeyBanc reports October 8Gb DDR5 DRAM contract pricing rose +12.0% M/M and +15.5% Q/Q, with DDR4 up +21.2% M/M and +35.7% Q/Q. AI datacenter demand is outpacing DRAM supply, with Samsung and MU expecting tight conditions into 2028 and SK Hynix into 2030. HBM4's >3x wafer ratio vs. DDR5 further constrains conventional DRAM supply. MU trades at only 4x consensus forward P/E vs. 3-year median of 9x; PT $1,750 on 6x FY28 EPS of $291.87.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure accelerated to 48% YoY growth, guided 49-50% in 2QFY27; $25B debt offering filed
bullets.body: Truist highlights Azure growth accelerating to 48% YoY in 1QFY27 from 43% in 4QFY26, with 2QFY27 guidance of 49-50%. GitHub Copilot Fusion now scores within 2 points of Claude Code Opus 5.5 Max at ~50% API cost and 40% faster execution. Separately, MSFT filed a $25B debt offering — its first IG bond issuance in over 9 years — to fund AI infrastructure investment. Hedgeye's McCullough removed MSFT from his long list.

bullets.title: ORCL: Launches $20B combined debt/equity raise; stock -3.3% pre-market
bullets.body: Oracle filed a $10B bond offering (six tranches, 2-20yr maturities) and $10B in common stock, reversing a prior commitment to limit gross debt growth to $10B through FY30. The combined $20B raise sent ORCL shares -3.3% in pre-market trading. The raise comes as hyperscaler AI-linked debt issuance has reached $655B YTD with projections for nearly $1T in new debt for 2027.

bullets.title: RDDT: Loop Capital downgrades to Hold, cuts PT to $100 from $250; DADCO maintains Buy at $125
bullets.body: Loop Capital cut RDDT to Hold from Buy with a PT reduction from $250 to $100 following the stock's -29% decline. DADCO (Bernstein) maintains Buy at $125 PT (cut from $185), arguing valuation at 8x 2027 EBITDA appears overdone; logged-in DAU engagement remains strong at 5x logged-out users and logged-in users represent >80% of monetization. Posts/comments reached 27B in 3Q (+1B QoQ). Near-term challenges remain but recovery thesis intact over 12-18 months.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 8 favorable — 77% favorites won; UBS maintains Buy
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on DraftKings after NFL Week 8 saw favorites win 10/13 games (77%), with 4/5 biggest moneyline favorites winning. This is the second week of eight where favorites won 75%+, versus typical 4.6 weeks per season. DKNG should see normal-to-higher hold. Jefferies Digital Gaming Summit Dec 3 in NYC includes DKNG 1x1 meetings.

bullets.title: BKNG: Q3 preview — consensus +5.9% gross bookings growth; 19/20 quarter EPS beat streak
bullets.body: Consensus expects BKNG Q3 gross bookings of $52.64B (+5.9% YoY, within guidance of +4-6%), revenue of $9.55B (+6.0%), EBITDA of $4.49B (+6.1%), and 340.45M room nights (+5.4%). Bull thesis: market-share dominance and strong FCF; bear thesis: slowing momentum and margin compression from direct marketing/AI spend. Stock up 23.5% since Aug 4; reports after close Nov 4.

bullets.title: EXPE: Q3 preview — 10.6% implied move; consensus $4.73B revenue, $8.85 EPS; reports 11/4
bullets.body: Expedia Q3 consensus expects $4.73B revenue (within guidance $4.65-4.75B), $1.55B EBITDA, and EPS of $8.85. Room nights consensus 111.85M (+4.0%). Stock up 6.7% since Aug 5 vs. S&P +1.1%. EXPE has beaten revenue consensus 15 of 20 quarters and EPS 17 of 20 quarters. Options imply ~10.6% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: XYZ (Block): Q3 preview — consensus $6.58B revenue, $1.03 EPS; options imply 10.5% move
bullets.body: Block reports Q3 after close on Nov 3. Consensus revenue is $6.58B and gross profit $3.16B vs. guidance $3.13B, with EPS of $1.03 vs. guidance $1.02. Cash App gross income expected $1.99B. Bulls cite Borrow pricing changes driving GP upside into 2027 and AI/product velocity supporting Rule of 50. Bears worry higher Borrow losses signal credit-quality deterioration and GP growth is decelerating to mid-teens.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi Buy maintained; Week 44 CCUs flat sequentially at 16.2M, implying 4Q bookings near top of guidance
bullets.body: Roblox Week 44 average peak CCUs were 16.2M, down 11% YoY but flat sequentially. Citi estimates this is consistent with 4Q bookings of $1.98B, at the high end of guidance ($1.89-2.0B) and slightly above Visible Alpha consensus of $1.97B. Hedgeye's McCullough removed RBLX from his long list.

bullets.title: APP: Citi Buy — US eCommerce client growth accelerating to 3.0% w/w in 4Q vs. 1.5% avg in 3Q
bullets.body: AppLovin has 20,387 global eCommerce clients as of Oct 30, up 6.0% week-over-week. US stores grew to 6,813, with weekly growth accelerating from 1.5% average in 3Q to 3.0% in 4Q QTD. APAC growth is even faster at 9.4% w/w but skewed toward lower-quality Hong Kong/China stores (now 45.6% of APAC). Citi maintains Buy. Citi hosting post-earnings call webcast Nov 4 at 7:30pm ET.

bullets.title: GEV: $20B buyback authorization approved; to acquire Trench Group for $9.0B
bullets.body: GE Vernova approved a $20B share repurchase authorization increase during the week of Oct 26. Separately, GEV announced it will acquire Trench Group for $9.0B per the StreetAccount M&A summary.

bullets.title: HF positioning: AI theme now net UW for first time since early 2023; tech correction in 'final innings' per MS
bullets.body: MS prime brokerage data shows hedge fund net exposure to the AI theme at 34% vs. 35.4% market cap weight — the first underweight since early 2023 — driven by negative earnings reactions across tech (INTC -29%, RDDT -29%, NOW -34%). Approximately 60% of Russell 3000 stocks are down 20%+ since June; cumulative degrossing exceeded 6% of HF book. MS's Mike Wilson says correction is in 'final innings.' Separately, McCullough's Hedgeye removed MSFT, RBLX, ROKU, and ABNB from longs; keeps AAPL and PLTR.
